steps.body: **Quadrilateral** is the umbrella club for every closed shape with four straight sides. Inside it live smaller clubs with stricter rules: the rectangle, the square, the rhombus, the trapezoid. One big family, many branches — each branch adds a rule.
Build a square by satisfying both the rectangle and rhombus rules.

widget.prompt: Build a square from attributes: four sides, four right angles, four equal sides, and two parallel pairs.
widget.successFeedback: A square satisfies both rule sets: it is a rectangle and a rhombus.
widget.sidesFeedback: Start inside the quadrilateral family with four sides.
widget.attributesFeedback: A square needs both four right angles and four equal sides, plus two parallel pairs.

predict.prompt: A square obeys the rectangle's rule AND adds more of its own. Does that make it a rectangle too?

options.label: Yes — meeting the rule means membership

predict.reveal: Shape clubs admit anyone who satisfies the rule — extra qualities don't disqualify. A square is a rectangle with a bonus, not a rival.

cml.actionGoal: Construct a square as the intersection of shape-family rules.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Change one non-defining attribute while preserving family membership. Which changes are legal?

explanation.prompt: Why can two shapes look different but belong to the same family?

options.label: They satisfy the same defining rules.
options.feedback: Yes — orientation and size are irrelevant to membership.

options.label: They must match one prototype picture.
options.feedback: A family includes every shape satisfying its rules.

explanationVariants: Four square corners but sides of different lengths is exactly the rectangle's rule — and not a square, since the sides aren't all equal.
Square corners → rectangle branch; unequal sides means it stops short of the square club.

widget.prompt: A four-sided shape has 4 square corners, but its length and width are different. What is it?

options.label: A rectangle
options.feedback: Four square corners is the rectangle rule — and unequal sides mean it's not the stricter square.

options.label: A square
options.feedback: A square also needs all four sides EQUAL. Different length and width keeps it in the rectangle club, not the square one.

options.label: A rhombus
options.feedback: A rhombus needs four EQUAL sides — this shape has different length and width. Its square corners make it a rectangle.

options.label: Just a quadrilateral, nothing more
options.feedback: It's a quadrilateral AND more — the four square corners earn it the rectangle name.

steps.body: The **trapezoid** joins the family with a gentler rule: at least one pair of parallel sides (two sides heading the same direction, like railroad tracks that never meet). It usually doesn't have square corners or equal sides — a looser branch, but still four sides, still a quadrilateral.

explanationVariants: One pair of parallel sides with no square corners and unequal sides fits the trapezoid, not the stricter branches.
Rectangles and rhombuses demand more; a single parallel pair is the trapezoid's calling card.

widget.prompt: A four-sided shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides, no square corners, and no equal sides. What is it?

options.label: A trapezoid
options.feedback: One parallel pair, and none of the stricter rules — that's the trapezoid branch.

options.label: A rectangle
options.feedback: A rectangle needs four SQUARE corners — this shape has none. One parallel pair points to the trapezoid.

options.label: A rhombus
options.feedback: A rhombus needs four EQUAL sides — this shape has none. Its single parallel pair makes it a trapezoid.

options.label: Not a quadrilateral at all
options.feedback: Four straight sides always means quadrilateral. This one's specific branch is the trapezoid.

widget.prompt: Sort each four-sided shape into its branch by the rules it follows.

items.label: 4 square corners, sides 6 and 3
items.feedback: Square corners, unequal sides — a rectangle.

items.label: 4 equal sides, corners tilted (not square)
items.feedback: Equal sides but no square corners — a rhombus (a 'pushed-over square').

items.label: One pair of parallel sides, nothing else equal
items.feedback: A single parallel pair — the trapezoid branch.

items.label: 4 square corners, sides 5 and 2
items.feedback: Square corners with unequal sides — another rectangle.

widget.missFeedback: Look for the branch rule: square corners → rectangle, equal sides → rhombus, one parallel pair → trapezoid.
widget.successFeedback: Two rectangles, one rhombus, one trapezoid — sorted by the rule each shape follows.

explanationVariants: Rectangle, rhombus, trapezoid, square — all have four straight sides, so all are quadrilaterals under the one umbrella.
The branch name adds rules, but every branch still meets the four-sided umbrella rule.

widget.prompt: Which of these is a quadrilateral: a rectangle, a rhombus, a trapezoid, or a square?

options.label: All of them — each has four straight sides
options.feedback: Every branch keeps the umbrella's rule of four sides, so all four are quadrilaterals.

options.label: Only the rectangle and square
options.feedback: The rhombus and trapezoid have four sides too — so they're also under the quadrilateral umbrella.

options.label: Only the trapezoid
options.feedback: The trapezoid qualifies, but so do the others — all four have four straight sides.

options.label: None — those are their own shapes
options.feedback: Being a rectangle doesn't cancel being a quadrilateral — the branch sits INSIDE the umbrella family.

hints: Check the strictest rules first: are all four corners square? Are all four sides equal?
Four equal sides but corners that aren't square — which branch guards equal sides?
explanationVariants: Four equal sides is the rhombus rule; because the corners aren't square, it isn't the stricter square. So: a rhombus.
Equal sides → rhombus branch; missing the square-corner rule keeps it out of the square club.

widget.prompt: A four-sided shape has 4 equal sides but its corners are NOT square (they're tilted). Which branch is it?

options.label: A rhombus
options.feedback: Four equal sides is the rhombus rule; tilted corners keep it out of the square club.

options.label: A square
options.feedback: A square also demands SQUARE corners — these are tilted. Equal sides alone make it a rhombus.

options.label: A rectangle
options.feedback: A rectangle demands square corners, which this shape lacks. Its equal sides point to the rhombus.

options.label: A trapezoid
options.feedback: A trapezoid's rule is one parallel pair, not four equal sides. Four equal sides is the rhombus.

takeaways: Quadrilateral is the umbrella: any closed 4-sided shape.
Rectangle = square corners; rhombus = equal sides; square = both; trapezoid = one parallel pair.
Branch names add rules, but every branch is still a quadrilateral.
steps.teaser: next: a shock — the square secretly belongs to the rectangle club.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Quadrilateral just means four sides** — it's the whole family. The special names (rectangle, rhombus, square, trapezoid) are branches, each with one extra rule. Count four straight sides first; then look for the extra rule to name the branch.

explanationVariants: Four square corners is the rectangle's rule.
Square corners with sides that can differ → rectangle branch.

widget.prompt: A 4-sided shape with 4 square corners (length ≠ width) is a…

options.label: Rectangle
options.feedback: Square corners → rectangle.

options.label: Triangle
options.feedback: A triangle has 3 sides — this has 4. Square corners make it a rectangle.

options.label: Rhombus
options.feedback: A rhombus needs equal sides; this has square corners instead — a rectangle.
